categories.name: AI Voice (Text to Speech)
categories.description: Text-to-speech APIs compared on the same public prompts: transcript accuracy, naturalness, instruction following, and speed.

metrics.label: Transcript accuracy
metrics.description: The audio is transcribed by an independent speech-recognition model and compared word-for-word with the prompt. 10 = zero word errors.

metrics.label: Naturalness
metrics.description: Predicted mean opinion score from a reference-free speech quality model (UTMOS / NISQA), rescaled to 1-10.

metrics.label: Instruction following
metrics.description: An LLM jury checks the transcript and audio metadata against the prompt's explicit constraints: language, pauses, digit-by-digit numbers, pronunciation notes, tone.

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.description: Time to first audio byte and total generation time, ranked against every other run in the category. 10 = fastest decile.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.description: Multilingual text-to-speech and voice cloning API, widely used for narration, dubbing and conversational agents.

tools.name: OpenAI TTS
tools.description: OpenAI's speech synthesis endpoint with steerable delivery via natural-language instructions.

tools.name: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech
tools.description: Google's managed TTS with Neural2, Studio and Chirp voices across many languages.

tools.name: Cartesia Sonic
tools.description: Low-latency streaming text-to-speech built for real-time voice agents.

tools.name: Amazon Polly
tools.description: AWS text-to-speech with standard, neural and generative voices and SSML control.

tools.name: Inworld TTS
tools.description: Inworld's text-to-speech API, built for real-time character and agent voices with low latency and expressive delivery.

tools.name: Kokoro-82M
tools.description: 82M-parameter open-weight TTS with 50+ preset voices across nine languages; runs many times faster than real time on a CPU through ONNX Runtime.

tools.name: Piper
tools.description: Fast VITS-based neural TTS built for the Raspberry Pi, with community voices in 30+ languages; the engine behind Home Assistant's local speech.

tools.name: KittenTTS Nano
tools.description: A 15M-parameter, 25 MB English TTS model with eight expressive preset voices, designed to run on any CPU without a GPU.

tools.name: SpeechT5 TTS
tools.description: Microsoft's unified speech-text transformer fine-tuned for English TTS, voiced through a HiFi-GAN vocoder and a CMU ARCTIC speaker embedding.

tools.name: MeloTTS
tools.description: Multilingual VITS-family TTS from MyShell with English (US, British, Indian, Australian), Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese and Korean models; real-time on CPU.

tools.name: XTTS-v2
tools.description: Coqui's 17-language voice-cloning TTS, now maintained by Idiap as coqui-tts; used here with a built-in studio speaker. Non-commercial licence (CPML).

tools.name: Parler-TTS Mini
tools.description: 880M-parameter English TTS steered by a natural-language description of the speaker and delivery; the only open model here that consumes the prompt's style instructions directly.

tools.name: Bark (small)
tools.description: Suno's generative audio transformer, small variant, with multilingual speaker presets; produces expressive speech but is slow on CPU and caps each generation at about 13 seconds.

tools.name: F5-TTS
tools.description: Flow-matching diffusion transformer TTS (v1 Base) that clones a short reference clip; English and Chinese training data. Weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0.

tools.name: Chatterbox Multilingual
tools.description: Resemble AI's 500M-parameter Llama-backbone TTS with emotion exaggeration control and 23 languages including Swedish; heavy on CPU.
